day_shape: Strait of Hormuz tanker struck by projectile with IRGC Navy claiming interception of a 'violating' vessel, Iran summons UK ambassador over RAF Fairford allegations, Houthi missiles intercepted toward Aramco in Dhahran, Trump says US decision on Iran 'very soon', IMF forecasts Iran GDP shrinking 7.6% in 2026.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker incident
threads.summary: UKMTO reported a projectile strike on a container ship in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran's Navy and IRGC Navy commander said a 'violating' tanker that had turned off tracking was intercepted and set alight east of the strait. IRGC Navy commander Azamayee said Americans should 'come closer' if they think the strait is open.

threads.label: UK-Iran diplomatic row over RAF Fairford
threads.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry summoned British Ambassador Hugo Shorter in Tehran to protest UK allegations attributing an incident at RAF Fairford to Iran. The Jerusalem Post cited the UK's domestic spy chief saying Iran is stepping up attempts to hit harder targets including military sites in Britain.

threads.label: US-Iran posture and renewed-strike talk
threads.summary: Trump told reporters a US 'decision on Iran very soon' is coming and said Washington may have gone 'too far' targeting Iranian leadership, while the Jerusalem Post reported Netanyahu discussed with Trump a possible renewed military campaign against Iran. The WSJ reported Iranian officials privately warned of land incursions into neighbouring countries if US strikes resume.

threads.label: Houthi strikes on Saudi Aramco
threads.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted Houthi missiles fired toward Aramco's Dhahran headquarters, and the Houthis declared Aramco oil facilities legitimate targets. Trump said the Houthis are 'behaving very badly' and that he will 'be there' after US midterm elections; Iran International cited analysts linking the attacks to Iranian aviation threats.

threads.label: Hezbollah rebuilding and Iranian cash flows
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Hezbollah is rebuilding military capabilities in southern Lebanon and upgrading explosive drones, and that Lebanese MPs are calling for a probe after hundreds of kilograms of Hezbollah explosives were found. Hezbollah announced up to $14,000 in housing aid following reports of a $200 million Iran transfer, a figure the US disputes.

threads.label: Iran domestic economy and unrest
threads.summary: The IMF forecast Iran's economy to shrink 7.6% in 2026, worse than Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Israel or Turkey, while Amnesty condemned the execution of five protest-linked prisoners in one week. Iran International reported gunfire and tear gas at a county-naming protest in central Iran and six killed in clashes near Zahedan.

threads.label: IDF operations in Gaza and West Bank
threads.summary: The IDF said it eliminated five Hamas and Islamic Jihad operatives in separate southern Gaza strikes, naming three PIJ operatives including a deputy squad commander and two Nukhba terrorists. Troops also apprehended four Islamic Jihad operatives in Qabatiya and Arraba in the northern West Bank following Shin Bet intelligence.

events.title_en: Zero to 100 plan for zero inflation by the Municipality, explained by Alireza Zekani: Alireza Zekani explained the 'zero inflation' plan from zero to 100 and said: An idea that I raised during the Martyr Raisi period in government was that in the 70s and especially the second half of the 90s, an approach based on making Tehran expensive to solve problems such as air pollution prevailed. Based on this class perspective, Tehran had to become so expensive that no one could live there. On the contrary, we believed that making things expensive not only failed to solve Tehran's problems, but drove people to the city's periphery and, by making Tehran a model for other parts of the country, extended high prices to the whole country; whilst Tehran's problems remained unresolved.
